purpose: Formal conformance substrate for idempotency-ref-v1. An external implementer who reproduces idempotency_ref byte-identical from the stated idempotency_artifact has a conformant implementation. idempotency_ref never enters the action_ref preimage.

vectors.description: pioneer-agent-001 submits payment.send with a client-generated idempotency_key and a 5-minute deduplication window (300000ms). A second submission with the same idempotency_artifact within the window MUST be detected as a duplicate. The COMMITTED record with this idempotency_ref is the canonical outcome.

invariants.idempotency_ref_not_in_preimage: idempotency_ref does not appear in action_preimage — action_ref determined solely by action_type, agent_id, scope, timestamp
invariants.independent_hashes: idempotency_ref = SHA-256(JCS(idempotency_artifact)); action_ref = SHA-256(JCS(action_preimage)); neither derived from the other
invariants.window_semantics: A PENDING record with this idempotency_ref older than window_ms (300000ms) from its timestamp is an orphaned-PENDING. window_ms elapsing is NOT evidence of outcome — orphaned-PENDING MUST NOT be treated as equivalent to FAILED unless the provider call itself carries a provider-enforced idempotency key (declared explicit, not assumed); default resolution is a provider-confirmed query, not a timer. The original record MUST NOT be mutated. (Corrected 2026-08-23, gap identified by impartshadow/agent-contracts, crewAIInc/crewAI#5802.)

notes.idempotency_key: Client-generated opaque string. Format is implementer-defined; only uniqueness within the deduplication window is required.
notes.window_ms: 300000ms = 5 minutes. Represents the deduplication window — not a TTL on the trail record itself.

vectors.description: NEGATIVE VECTOR (Invariant 5). crew-runtime-agent-042 attempts payment.send for the same intended refund twice: attempt 1 fails a guardrail and re-enters via the model, which regenerates the tool-call arguments (memo field reworded, amount unchanged) before retry. A non-conformant implementation derives idempotency_key as sha256(JCS(regenerated_args)) — because the two attempts' arguments differ in wording, the two idempotency_ref values do NOT collide, so equality-based deduplication never fires and both attempts commit as distinct effects (two refunds for the same order). This is the class of gap named by vasilisnasopoulos (crewAIInc/crewAI#5802, comment 5462928784) and independently cross-verified by mstevens843/crashpoint (2490 crash+recover trials against LangGraph/Temporal/DBOS, all three needed a fifth DIVERGED outcome for exactly this non-reproducibility). A conformant implementation instead derives idempotency_key from a durable, caller-assigned identifier fixed BEFORE the model runs (here, the order id) — see attempt_conformant.

attempt_2_non_conformant.vs_attempt_1: idempotency_ref DIFFERS from attempt_1 despite identical intent (same order, same amount) — memo wording changed on regeneration. Dedup by equality never fires; both attempts commit as separate effects. This is the bug the negative vector demonstrates.

attempt_conformant.derivation_note: idempotency_key = 'req_' + the caller's own pre-execution request id + order id — fixed before either model attempt ran, identical for both attempt_1 and attempt_2's underlying intent, so a retry with regenerated arguments produces the SAME idempotency_ref both times and dedup fires correctly.

invariants.invariant_5_durable_derivation: idempotency_key MUST derive from inputs fixed before the model runs for that attempt, never from the model's regenerated output for that attempt. Hashing tool-call arguments that a guardrail retry can reword is non-conformant even though the derivation mechanics (JCS+SHA-256) are followed correctly — Invariant 5 constrains what may feed the hash, not how the hash is computed.
